newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court jails two over deadly spa blaze.
newsitem.headline: French court jails two over deadly spa blaze.

text.p: A court jailed the director and the architect of a health spa in southern France for six months on Wednesday over a blaze in which 21 people died.
The Toulouse court gave eight other defendants suspended sentences on charges of causing death or injury by negligence or failure to respect safety rules at the Barbotan-les-Thermes baths.
It cleared three of the 13 defendants of any role in the June 1991 blaze that killed 20 bathers, most of them elderly or handicapped people stranded in water or thick mud, and a nurse.
The blaze was accidentally triggered by workers using hot tar to repair the roof of the four-year old building, set in rolling countryside.
The spa's managing director Joseph Couybes and its architect, Edmond Lay, got the stiffest punishments, of six months in jail and another 18 months suspended.
